rendered: In S. marcescens H32, Sun et al. introduced a water-forming NADH oxidase, encoded by[1]nox from Lactobacillus brevis[2], i.e. the enzyme was taken from a lactic acid bacterium rather than from S. marcescens itself. Oxidizing NADH to water shifted the cell's redox balance:[3][4]increasing the NAD^+/NADH ratio by 2.9-fold and redirecting flux[5] toward acetoin. This works because NADH is needed for the dehydrogenase step that reduces acetoin to the diol, as the review notes:[6]acetoin, and reduced to 2,3-BD by 2,3-butanediol dehydrogenase (BDH)[7], so draining NADH favors accumulation of the oxidized product. In fed-batch fermentation the engineered strain produced[8]75.2 g L[9]^-1 acetoin, while the by-product fell:[10]2,3-BD decreasing by ~52%[11]. The same case is listed in the strain table as the cofactor-engineering entry[12]H32 → H32-nox[13], with a fermentation time in hours of[14]40[15] and a titer in mg per liter of[16]75,200[17]; see[18] Table 2[19].
